extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, Technology Center leadership, OPQA staff, and external patent stakeholders (applicants, practitioners, top-filing firms)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for producing reliable, durable patents through examiner training and resourcing, OPQA monitoring and reviews, data-driven sampling and measurement, stakeholder collaboration, and targeted improvement plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide high-quality examination of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide high-quality examination of patent applications to issue reliable and durable patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching mission statement driving examiner training, resources, monitoring and collaboration efforts. All other activities (expertise, resources, monitoring, collaboration) support this primary goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: New examiner training — Initial residency in Patent Training Academy (PTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small groups of newly hired examiners organized by technology; moving toward an 8 week program; purpose to integrate new examiners into their art units earlier; 320 hours per examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 40 hours for onboarding and orientation; approximately 280 hours of formal training practicing prosecution techniques and independent and group work/discussions; 120 courses providing patentability statutes and examiner tools training (accessing applications, searching, and Office action writing).

rubrics_metrics.name: New examiner training — Residency within the Technology Center (TC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hands-on training: start examining applications under the mentorship and guidance of their SPE while working in the assigned art unit and examining specific technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to 37 additional hours of training on topics specific to the TC (e.g., sequence rule compliance, searching exercises, blockchain technology). Formal PTA-provided training supplements with 32 courses; 58 hours covering topics later in prosecution (managing amendments, finality practice, declaration practice, appeals practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Progression to Primary Examiner — required legal training and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to progress to Primary Examiner include legal coursework and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Law and Evidence Coursework: 40-hour course covering authoritative court decisions on statutory issues; certifications include negotiation authority and legal competency; Signatory authority program (~18 months) involving intensive review of at least 34 Office actions; paths include Partial and Full Signatory Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Examiner responsibilities and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary Examiner: delegated authority to determine patentability of applications and serve as a subject matter expert and coach/mentor to assistant examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiners are responsible for signatory authority where applicable and mentoring non-primary examiners; they play a frontline role in quality through decisions and supervisory interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing education for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing corps-wide and TC-level training to maintain and update examiner knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes training based on new court decisions, guidance, statutes/rules; TC-implemented initiatives tied to quality impact plans; Technical Training on Demand (TTOD) with 600+ courses covering all utility TCs; non-duty hour technical and legal trainings at credited colleges/universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner supervisory and subject-matter resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SPEs and SMEs as frontline quality mechanisms providing coaching, mentoring, QA meetings, and points-of-contact for special issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPEs shift administrative duties to focus on review of examiner’s work, conduct quality enhancement meetings and art unit level trainings. SMEs include experienced examiners, Quality Assurance Specialists, appeals specialists, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office resources outside TCs to support examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Central offices provide specialized legal, search/translation, and QA support to examining corps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Office of Patent Legal Administration (develops rules/practices and trains examiners on legal issues), Scientific & Technical Information Center (assists on search and translation), Office of Patent Quality Assurance (assessment, coaching, quality reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern examiner tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide state-of-the-art search tools and robust IT infrastructure to improve prior art identification and examination processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes AI-based tools such as Similarity Search, More Like This Document, Reverse Image Search pilot; modernization of processes and IT to increase likelihood of identifying best prior art early in prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA independent and unbiased assessment mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA conducts independent and unbiased assessment of TC work product to support issuance of reliable, durable patents and evidence-based decisions across the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffed with subject matter experts skilled at statistics, legal analysis, technology and reviewing; monitors and analyzes multi-source data to identify leading indicators of compliance issues; collaborates with TCs to improve efficiencies, minimize rework, and support compact prosecution; statutorily mandated to supply patent quality data to Congress (35 U.S.C. § 13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory compliance standard for Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When rejecting a claim, the Office’s patentability determination must be correct and must, at a minimum, identify the claim and relevant statute and set forth sufficient evidence to put a person skilled in the art on notice why the claim is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an allowed claim, the Office action must not omit a statutorily compliant rejection. Correctness is considered through the lens of whether determinations were reasonable and not based on what the reviewer would have done in the first instance. Statutory compliance supports reliability and durability of issued patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA review outcomes and TC interaction process
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA completes reviews, informs the TC, and outcomes include passthrough, attention needed, or noncompliance; TCs may rebut OPQA noncompliance findings and take corrective action as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow: OPQA completes a review → informs TC → TC considers feedback (passthrough/attention needed/noncompliance) → TC may rebut → OPQA reconsiders based on TC rebuttal → TC manages feedback and, if noncompliance maintained, takes appropriate corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective sampling methodology for statutory compliance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Design sampling to achieve strong statistical confidence for Corps-wide and TC-level estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with minimally acceptable corps-wide sample based on total Office actions mailed aiming for 95% confidence interval with margin of error ±0.5% (achievable with ~5,900 reviews corps-wide). Adjust for TC precision at 95% CI with margin ±1.5% (≈656 reviews per smallest TC). Allocate sampling by TC proportional to Office actions mailed; extrapolate smallest-TC sample up to corps (e.g., 656/8% → 8,200 reviews). Expand sample to ~12,000 to achieve adequate precision for rarer topics (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 101 rejections comprising ~7% of actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce data with strong confidence and granularity
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA's random reviewing scheme should achieve strong confidence intervals at Corps and TC levels and produce a minable dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheme yields minable dataset of approximately 1,000,000 individual data points to assess patent examination quality from many angles; sampling error information is tracked and reported by TC/statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPQA internal quality controls and feedback loops
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA ensures its own review quality through TC feedback, internal consistency reviews, and regular meetings between OPQA Quality Leads and TC representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency reviews and discussions occur within technologies and across OPQA; discussions with OPLA and TCs are used as needed to align handling of statutes/subject matter and specific cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frontline supervisory review and interaction to ensure examiner quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular supervisor reviews of examiner workproduct with detailed one-on-one feedback are essential to ensuring examiner quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistant examiners have all Office actions reviewed and signed by a supervisor or authorized primary examiner; primary examiners have regular discussions with supervisors and performance rating reviews; use appeal/pre-appeal conferences and consider PTAB decisions in discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of process measures and data analytics to monitor quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage data analytics and multiple data sources to identify risk areas, track efficiencies, and detect inconsistent examiner behaviors indicative of quality concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor transactional data and other sources; strategically focus reviews on areas of highest risk and inconsistency to efficiently allocate QA resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception surveys as leading quality indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct internal and external stakeholder perception surveys semi-annually to validate alignment of quality metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External survey directed to perceptions on correctness, clarity and consistency of examiner work product (sample ~3,150 top-filing customers; panel design with stratified random selection). Internal survey administered to examiners focusing on factors impacting ability to provide high-quality examination (tools, training, coaching/mentoring). Surveys serve as vital leading indicators and validation of other quality metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving work product through root cause analysis and tailored solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use assessment data to identify quality trends and underlying causes, then implement tailored solutions to improve compliance, reduce rework, and promote efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify best practices, implement targeted interventions (training, process changes, motivation/resources). Root cause analysis should inform whether training or other levers are most appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Quality Impact Plans — targeted, multifaceted improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology Centers regularly evaluate data at multiple levels and develop targeted and tailored improvement plans in collaboration with training, OPQA, SMEs and policy divisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach is multifaceted: training is not always the answer — also focus on improving processes, increasing motivation, and leveraging/improving resources. Plans operate at Corps, Discipline, TC, and Art Unit levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of high-quality examination (Accolade letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA identifies high-quality work during reviews and issues Accolade letters for consistent use of best practices or work that goes above and beyond typical examination practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accolade letters specify the best practices exemplified or reference reviewer’s specific accolade comments and are delivered to frontline supervisors for presentation to the examiner; metrics reported on percent of compliant reviews receiving accolades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnering with external stakeholders — Application readiness and public training
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with applicants to provide practice tips and training to enable filing strong applications that facilitate high-quality prosecution and support examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO offers training for the public (StART, STEPP, CLE, Patent Pro Bono, Inventor Assistance Center, Pre-application assessment program, guidance documents). High-quality applications and disclosure of relevant information aid search and prosecution quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide up-to-date, accessible resources and regional outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain online and in-person resources across the country to support applicants and examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key resources include Public Learning Center, Examination Guidance and Training Materials, Quality Metrics pages, Patent Examiner Technical Training Program, Patent Legal Administration pages, regional outreach offices, community outreach offices, and Patent and Trademark Resource Centers (PTRCs).
